question: Which of these is an example of objective data you can collect during an emotional assessment?

options.A: Observed body posture and facial expressions
options.B: The patient's dream journal from last year
options.C: What the patient's family members whisper outside
options.D: The patient's private personal feelings about God

explanation: Objective data means things you can physically see, hear, or measure yourself—like slumped shoulders, a crying face, or restless hands.

question: How soon can a person's fertility return after an abortion procedure?

options.A: After exactly six months
options.B: Not for at least two years
options.C: As early as two weeks
options.D: Only after menopause begins

explanation: Surprise! Ovulation can bounce back in as little as two weeks. That's why talking about family planning early is so crucial before she leaves the clinic. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of a Glucose Tolerance Test?

options.A: To measure how the body clears a glucose load over time
options.B: To evaluate how quickly the kidneys filter sugar from the blood
options.C: To measure the exact amount of insulin stored in the pancreas
options.D: To determine the average blood sugar level over the past three months

explanation: The GTT tracks how effectively the body processes and clears a specific amount of glucose over several hours. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h1)

question: Which of these is a critical warning sign that a patient with an ovarian cyst should report right away?

options.A: A slight increase in clear vaginal discharge
options.B: Mild bloating right before her monthly period
options.C: Sudden, severe, and worsening abdominal pain
options.D: Feeling tired after a long day at work

explanation: Severe pain that comes out of nowhere is a red flag for dangerous complications like a cyst bursting or twisting (torsion). Always take it seriously!

question: Why is it important to pick the right statistical test for your research data?

options.A: Patients will refuse to take their medications if the math is wrong
options.B: Ethical boards will fine the nursing unit for messy spreadsheets
options.C: Using the wrong test can lead to false conclusions and bad clinical practices
options.D: Hospital computers will crash if you select an improper formula

explanation: Right on target. Different questions need different math tools; using the wrong one gives misleading answers that could affect patient care.

question: What is the main reason developing countries experience more complications from unsafe injections?

options.A: A complete lack of trained nurses in regional clinics
options.B: Patients refusing oral medications in favor of injections
options.C: The natural resistance of tropical germs to standard soap
options.D: Supply shortages and poor waste management systems

explanation: Exactly. When clinics struggle with equipment shortages, it can unfortunately lead to dangerous workarounds like reusing syringes. You're building great clinical awareness! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h2)

question: What does empowerment mean in the context of community mobilisation?

options.A: Building local capacity to solve health problems independently
options.B: Giving financial loans to every household in the village
options.C: Allowing nurses to make all decisions without community input
options.D: Handing out free medicine during festival seasons

explanation: Empowerment equips community members with the skills and confidence to address their own health challenges long-term. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is the main difference between short-acting and long-acting beta-2 agonists?

options.A: Short-acting drugs are used for COPD, while long-acting drugs are only for asthma
options.B: Short-acting drugs are taken as pills, while long-acting drugs can only be injected
options.C: Short-acting drugs give quick relief during attacks, while long-acting drugs provide daily maintenance
options.D: Short-acting drugs reduce inflammation, while long-acting drugs only relax muscles

explanation: Short-acting drugs are your quick-fix rescue inhalers for sudden tightness, while long-acting drugs work quietly in the background all day to keep airways open.

question: Why can no single agency handle a major disaster completely on its own?

options.A: Government rules forbid any agency from working alone
options.B: Agencies prefer to wait for outside help before starting
options.C: Individual organizations lack any trained leadership staff
options.D: No single agency has all the necessary resources and expertise

explanation: Major emergencies overwhelm the capacity of any single group, making teamwork across various sectors necessary for survival and recovery. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h1)

question: If a nurse wants to reach tech-savvy urban youth to talk about waste management, what is the best channel?

options.A: Printed paper leaflets
options.B: Medical textbooks
options.C: Town criers
options.D: Social media

explanation: Spot on! Young people in cities spend a lot of time online, making social media the fastest way to get them talking and taking action.

question: A student struggles heavily with handwriting, spacing words, and holding a pencil firmly. Which condition fits these signs best?

options.A: Dysgraphia
options.B: Dyscalculia
options.C: Aphasia
options.D: Dyslexia

explanation: Dysgraphia directly interferes with the physical and mental processes of writing and putting thoughts onto paper. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h2)

question: A patient with Parkinson's disease is at high risk for falls. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Implement a comprehensive fall prevention plan and clear walking paths
options.B: Keep the patient strictly confined to bedrest at all times
options.C: Remove all supportive walking aids to force independent balance
options.D: Encourage the patient to run down hospital hallways for exercise

explanation: Stiffness and a shuffling gait mean falls are a real danger. Keeping pathways clear and taking smart safety precautions helps protect your patient while keeping them mobile.

question: What is a major challenge when doing sterile procedures in a patient's home?

options.A: Finding a completely clean surface to set up sterile equipment
options.B: Needing a specialized hospital operating table for every task
options.C: Preventing family members from assisting with the procedure
options.D: Having too many doctors present during the dressing change

explanation: Spot on! Houses don't come pre-sterilized like hospital rooms. As a nurse, you have to create your own clean barrier to keep your sterile supplies safe from everyday household surfaces.

question: What is a common clinical consequence for nurses when the health sector is chronically underfunded?

options.A: Higher salaries and improved workplace safety standards
options.B: An abundance of modern diagnostic equipment on every ward
options.C: Decreased patient wait times in accident and emergency units
options.D: Severe burnout from heavy patient-to-staff ratios

explanation: Underfunding means fewer staff and fewer resources, leaving the nurses on duty to handle overwhelming patient crowds. Burnout is a very real challenge here!

question: What is the main job of minerals like sodium and potassium in our bodies?

options.A: Regulating fluid balance and supporting nerve and muscle function
options.B: Acting as organic enzymes to speed up chemical digestion
options.C: Providing the structural framework for red blood cell hemoglobin
options.D: Serving as the body's primary emergency source of stored calories

explanation: Correct! Electrolytes like sodium and potassium keep our body fluids balanced and help our nerves and muscles work smoothly without cramping.

question: Why should nurses check and document what is left on a patient's meal tray rather than just taking it away?

options.A: To speed up the collection of dirty kitchen dishes
options.B: To calculate the precise cost of hospital food items
options.C: To ensure accurate tracking of actual calories consumed
options.D: To prevent patients from sharing food with visitors

explanation: An empty tray doesn't always mean the patient ate the food! Direct observation helps us chart their true nutritional intake accurately.

question: What should you do when a clear-headed home care patient refuses a necessary treatment?

options.A: Ask family members to pressure the patient into agreeing
options.B: Educate on the risks, respect the choice, and document the refusal
options.C: Immediately discharge the patient from the home care agency
options.D: Administer the treatment anyway to prevent complications

explanation: Well done! Always give them the facts so they understand the risks, but remember: competent adults have the final say over their own bodies.

question: What is the main goal of community-based accident prevention programs?

options.A: Building larger trauma wards in every city
options.B: Stopping accidents before they happen through education
options.C: Increasing the supply of emergency surgical gloves
options.D: Training more mortuary attendants

explanation: Prevention is all about spotting risks early and educating the public so accidents never happen in the first place.

question: What is the main goal of modern patient safety design in healthcare?

options.A: To make doing the right thing easy and mistakes difficult
options.B: To eliminate all forms of human emotion from clinical work
options.C: To hide medical errors from patients and their families
options.D: To punish nurses severely whenever an adverse event occurs

explanation: Spot on! Good hospital design sets up simple workflows that naturally guide us to do the right thing every time.

question: Which patient sign means you should grab and attach an AED right away?

options.A: Severe chest pain and heavy sweating
options.B: Confusion and mild shortness of breath
options.C: High fever and a rapid pulse rate
options.D: Unresponsiveness and no normal breathing

explanation: An AED is meant for sudden cardiac arrest. We look for someone who has collapsed, doesn't respond, and isn't breathing normally.

question: What is the main reason pregnant women get carpal tunnel syndrome in the third trimester?

options.A: A sudden tumor growth inside the carpal tunnel space
options.B: Permanent calcium deficiency destroying the bones of the wrist
options.C: Severe inflammation caused by repetitive typing work
options.D: Fluid retention causing tissue swelling that compresses the median nerve

explanation: Extra body fluid in late pregnancy swells the tissues inside the tight wrist space, pressing on the median nerve. Simple as that!

question: How often should you change a clean, intact transparent IV dressing?

options.A: Every 24 hours
options.B: Every 7 days
options.C: Only when the IV line is removed
options.D: Every 14 days

explanation: Standard hospital guidelines recommend changing transparent peripheral IV dressings every 7 days unless they get dirty, loose, or wet.

question: A nurse administrator checks a mobile medical unit. Which action best shows readiness for action?

options.A: Ordering excess supplies to fill every available inch of storage space
options.B: Relying entirely on local cellular networks for all emergency communication
options.C: Waiting until a disaster is officially declared before checking equipment
options.D: Verifying that supply carts and trauma kits match standardized inventory checklists

explanation: Using checklists ensures that every essential drug and piece of trauma gear is present and fully functional before deployment.

question: Two clinical nurses independently score a patient's wound healing using the same chart. What type of reliability are they testing?

options.A: Parallel forms reliability
options.B: Test-retest reliability
options.C: Inter-rater reliability
options.D: Internal consistency reliability

explanation: Since two separate raters are checking their agreement on the same patient, it's inter-rater reliability in action!

question: What is the primary function of plasmin during the healing process?

options.A: It breaks down and dissolves the fibrin clot
options.B: It stimulates the rapid production of new platelets
options.C: It causes the initial vascular spasm in injured vessels
options.D: It converts inactive prothrombin into active thrombin

explanation: Plasmin is the active enzyme responsible for digesting fibrin strands so the body can clear away old, unneeded clots. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h5)

question: A client wants a refill for her birth control, but admits she might already be pregnant. What should you do first?

options.A: Perform a pregnancy test before giving the refill
options.B: Tell her to double her dose for the next week
options.C: Switch her to a progestin-only pill right away
options.D: Refill the prescription immediately without questions

explanation: Safety first! Always rule out an existing pregnancy before continuing hormonal contraceptives to protect both the client and potential pregnancy.

question: A nurse arrives at a patient's home for a dressing change. What is the very first action the nurse should take regarding the visiting kit?

options.A: Ask the patient to wash the stethoscope with soap
options.B: Place a protective paper lining on a surface and set the bag on it
options.C: Put the used dressing materials directly inside the main bag
options.D: Open the bag and pull out the forceps immediately

explanation: Setting down a protective barrier before placing the bag protects the kit from picking up contamination from furniture or tables. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h4)

question: How is Ultra-High Temperature (UHT) milk different from standard pasteurized milk?

options.A: UHT milk contains chemical preservatives instead of heat treatment
options.B: UHT milk can remain shelf-stable at room temperature until opened
options.C: UHT milk is boiled slowly on a stove for several hours
options.D: UHT milk requires continuous refrigeration from farm to table

explanation: Brilliant! UHT uses super high heat that wipes out practically all microbes, meaning you can store it on your shelf without a fridge until you pop it open.

question: What was the original main goal of introducing Universal Precautions?

options.A: Ensuring accurate diagnosis of chronic illnesses
options.B: Speeding up the admission process for new patients
options.C: Protecting health workers from bloodborne pathogens
options.D: Lowering the overall cost of hospital equipment

explanation: Universal Precautions were originally created specifically to shield healthcare staff from infections transmitted through blood and specific body fluids. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h1)

question: How does a mild fever actually help your body fight an infection?

options.A: It stops the heart from pumping blood to sick tissues.
options.B: It flushes germs out entirely through the sweat glands.
options.C: It speeds up metabolism and helps white blood cells work better.
options.D: it melts the cell walls of harmful bacteria directly.

explanation: A controlled fever creates a hostile environment for germs while boosting your immune cells so they can do their job faster!

question: A patient comes to the clinic with a fever and headache, but is fully alert and able to swallow drugs. How do you classify this?

options.A: Asymptomatic malaria
options.B: Chronic malaria
options.C: Severe malaria
options.D: Uncomplicated malaria

explanation: Correct! Because the patient is stable and can take oral meds without danger signs, it's uncomplicated malaria. You'll see this a lot in clinical postings!

question: A nurse notices that a medication dose for postpartum bleeding is written unclearly on the chart. What is the safest immediate action?

options.A: Clarify the order with the prescribing doctor before giving the drug
options.B: Guess the correct dosage based on the patient's general appearance
options.C: Skip the medication dose entirely without telling anyone
options.D: Administer the medication quickly to avoid wasting valuable time

explanation: You nailed it! Never guess when administering drugs. Verifying unclear orders protects both your license and your patient from harm.

question: Which client should you, as a nurse, keep a close eye on for signs of complicated grief?

options.A: A client who cries openly while talking about a loved one during the first week after a death
options.B: A client who expresses persistent bitterness and an inability to accept a sudden loss many months later
options.C: A client who finds comfort in sharing memories of the deceased with close friends
options.D: A client who participates in traditional funeral and memorial services

explanation: Spot on! Holding onto deep bitterness and refusing to accept the reality months down the track are red flags for complicated grief.

question: What is the absolute first priority when managing any acute poisoning patient in the emergency unit?

options.A: Securing the airway and ensuring adequate breathing
options.B: Collecting urine samples for toxicological screening
options.C: Inducing immediate vomiting to empty the stomach
options.D: Administering activated charcoal via nasogastric tube

explanation: Always fall back on your ABCDEs! Life support and stabilization always come way before diagnostic tests or trying to remove the poison.

question: Why is cardiac syncope considered the most dangerous type of fainting?

options.A: It is almost impossible to diagnose with standard hospital equipment.
options.B: It causes permanent brain damage within just a few seconds.
options.C: It is frequently linked to serious heart rhythm problems or structural disease.
options.D: It only happens when the patient is actively exercising or working.

explanation: Cardiac syncope stems from heart issues that carry a high risk of sudden cardiac arrest if left untreated. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h2)

question: What is the main focus of custodial care?

options.A: Performing emergency surgeries and acute trauma procedures
options.B: Administering complex intravenous medications and therapies
options.C: Providing non-medical help with daily living and personal needs
options.D: Curing acute infections through targeted antibiotic therapy

explanation: Custodial care is entirely non-medical and centers on helping people manage their routine daily needs rather than curing active diseases. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h1)

question: Why are immunization and antenatal clinics such great places to teach mothers about nutrition?

options.A: Doctors perform surgical procedures to improve digestion during these visits
options.B: Patients have extra money to spend on luxury foods when visiting the clinic
options.C: Hospitals provide free meals to every single visitor who walks through the door
options.D: They bring mothers and vulnerable young children into regular contact with nurses

explanation: You got it! Routine clinic visits give us the perfect chance to reach and educate the exact people who need nutritional guidance the most.

question: What is the main goal when public health workers investigate a sudden disease outbreak?

options.A: To punish individuals who failed to maintain hygiene
options.B: To document medical billing records for the hospital
options.C: To manufacture new vaccines for the infected population
options.D: To find the exact source and stop the outbreak from spreading

explanation: Detective work is a huge part of nursing! Finding the source quickly lets health teams step in and protect the rest of the community.

question: You are plotting patient age on the X-axis and length of stay on the Y-axis. After drawing your blank axes, what is next?

options.A: Erase the axis labels to make the chart look cleaner
options.B: Calculate the percentage of patients over the age of sixty
options.C: Draw a straight line connecting every single dot in order
options.D: Scale the axes with equal intervals to fit the data values

explanation: Before plotting dots, you need to set up your numbers evenly along the axes so your graph is accurate and easy to read.

question: Which spinal nerve roots combine to form the brachial plexus?

options.A: T1 through T12
options.B: C5 through T1
options.C: C1 through C4
options.D: L1 through S4

explanation: The brachial plexus is a complex web formed by the ventral rami of cervical nerves five through eight and the first thoracic nerve. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h5)

question: Why does an inflamed cervix tend to bleed easily during an examination?

options.A: Complete destruction of the underlying muscle layer
options.B: Fragile tissues and tiny blood vessels opening up from inflammation
options.C: Rapid overproduction of red blood cells by the cervix
options.D: Severe blood clotting disorders throughout the body

explanation: When tissue is inflamed, blood rushes to the area and the vessels become delicate, meaning even a gentle touch can cause spotting.

question: When is the best time to talk about end-of-life wishes and care planning with the family?

options.A: As early in the disease trajectory as possible
options.B: When the patient develops sudden aspiration pneumonia
options.C: Immediately after the final post-mortem examination
options.D: Only after the patient becomes completely mute and bedbound

explanation: Having these conversations early lets the patient share what they want while they still can, making future medical choices much easier for everyone involved.

question: As a student nurse, what is your main personal duty when it comes to hospital waste guidelines?

options.A: To prosecute scavengers who enter hospital grounds
options.B: To manufacture color-coded waste bags for the facility
options.C: To comply with disposal protocols and protect patients and staff from hazards
options.D: To design the hospital's waste incinerator plant

explanation: You are on the front lines! Following waste disposal rules every single day is one of the best ways you can keep your patients, your colleagues, and yourself safe.

question: How does evaluation help ensure the sustainability of a health project?

options.A: It allows the government to stop sending free medical supplies
options.B: It proves that nurses no longer need to visit the village
options.C: It forces community leaders to take full financial blame for failures
options.D: It proves to the community that their hard work is producing results

explanation: Seeing tangible improvements encourages the community to keep up their healthy behaviors for the long term. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why must you discard a sterile syringe pack if the paper seal is torn?

options.A: The manufacturer will refuse to replace the item
options.B: The expiration date is instantly reset to zero
options.C: The sterile barrier is broken, risking patient infection
options.D: The plastic inside will automatically melt in the air

explanation: A torn pack means outside air and germs have gotten in. Even if it looks clean, that sterile seal is gone, making it unsafe to use.

question: Which of these tasks is an example of an Instrumental Activity of Daily Living (IADL)?

options.A: Eating a prepared meal
options.B: Bathing independently
options.C: Managing household finances
options.D: Dressing in the morning

explanation: Great job! Instrumental activities are the slightly more complex tasks needed to manage a household, like shopping, cooking, and handling money.

question: Which of these is NOT a common reason why nurses resist workplace change?

options.A: Cynicism caused by past failed projects
options.B: Fear of appearing incompetent with new technology
options.C: Desire to increase overall patient hospital stays
options.D: Fatigue from working understaffed shifts

explanation: You got this! Nurses resist due to fear, fatigue, or routine disruption, but nobody wants patients staying in the hospital longer than needed.

question: What are the common signs of Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia in someone with advanced HIV?

options.A: Severe throat pain and difficulty swallowing
options.B: Sudden chest pain and sharp pleuritic discomfort
options.C: Progressive dry cough and shortness of breath
options.D: Productive cough with rust-colored sputum

explanation: This opportunistic infection usually starts slowly with a dry cough, low fever, and trouble breathing during activity.

question: A patient is scheduled for an abdominal CT with IV contrast. What is the very first thing a nurse should check?

options.A: Administer a full dose of oral laxatives to clear the bowel
options.B: Assess the patient for a history of seafood or iodine allergies
options.C: Shave the hair on the patient's abdomen near the umbilicus
options.D: Insert an indwelling urinary catheter for continuous output

explanation: Safety first! Checking for allergies prevents severe reactions to the iodine contrast. You are thinking like a real nurse!

question: Why is the IASC framework designed as a pyramid rather than a square?

options.A: To illustrate that basic community needs affect a larger population than specialized care
options.B: To prove that physical safety is less important than psychiatric medications
options.C: To show that specialized services are needed by the majority of the population
options.D: To demonstrate that doctors must handle every level of community distress

explanation: Think of it like a crowd: the wide base at the bottom represents everyday survival needs that affect almost everyone, while the narrow top shows specialized care needed by fewer people.

question: What does 'voluntary participation' mean when recruiting study participants?

options.A: Participants must be paid a large cash reward for joining the study
options.B: Patients must complete all questionnaires before leaving the hospital ward
options.C: Hospital management decides which patients are best suited for the study
options.D: Patients can choose to join or refuse without facing any negative consequences

explanation: Brilliant! Participation must always be completely free choice—no penalties, no pressure.

question: What does it mean if a placenta is described as a 'battledore placenta'?

options.A: A placenta with a thick white ring on its edge
options.B: A placenta split into two equal-sized lobes
options.C: A placenta where the umbilical cord inserts at the margin
options.D: A placenta with an accessory lobe nearby

explanation: Think of a battledore insertion like a tennis racket handle attached right at the edge of the disk instead of the middle. Easy to picture once you see it! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h2)

question: What is the best nursing response when a patient believes their blood disorder is caused entirely by spiritual forces?

options.A: Report the family to hospital security for refusing modern medicine
options.B: Ignore their cultural belief completely and talk only about drugs
options.C: Respect their beliefs while gently providing education on the medical condition
options.D: Scold the patient and family for holding unscientific ideas

explanation: Respect builds trust! When patients feel heard, they are much more willing to listen to your medical guidance.

question: Why is writing prompt and accurate patient notes so important in home health care?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for verbal handovers to colleagues
options.B: It stops family members from asking questions about the patient
options.C: It serves as your legal proof of the care and assessments you provided
options.D: It guarantees you will get paid on time by health insurance

explanation: Exactly! In nursing, if it wasn't charted, it wasn't done. Good notes protect both you and the patient.

question: Which of these specimens should NOT be put in the refrigerator if transport is delayed?

options.A: Routine urine collection
options.B: Swab of a skin wound
options.C: Stool sample for parasites
options.D: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)

explanation: CSF contains very delicate germs that the cold can easily kill. These urgent samples need to stay at room temperature!

question: Why is keeping a look-out for fire hazards trickier in a patient's house compared to a hospital ward?

options.A: Private homes are always built using highly flammable wood
options.B: Hospitals have stricter rules against using electricity
options.C: Nurses have no legal authority to check home environments
options.D: Private homes have unpredictable layouts and lack institutional safety systems

explanation: Hospitals have built-in alarms, sprinklers, and standard designs. Every patient's home is different and usually lacks these heavy-duty safety backups.

question: What is the heart of equity in healthcare financing?

options.A: Private hospitals should receive more government subsidies than public clinics
options.B: Access to care should be based on health needs rather than the ability to pay
options.C: Every citizen must pay an identical flat fee for hospital registration
options.D: Urban residents must have priority access to surgical specialists

explanation: Equity is about fairness. Your wallet shouldn't decide whether you live or die.

question: Why must a nurse view pharmacotherapy as a balance between benefits and risks?

options.A: Therapeutic effects only occur when toxic reactions are actively triggered
options.B: Patients will refuse treatment if they know about any potential side effects
options.C: Every medication carries some level of inherent hazard alongside its healing properties
options.D: Hospital policies require reporting all minor medication side effects daily

explanation: All drugs have the potential to cause harm, so nurses must weigh therapeutic gains against possible toxic effects. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h1)

question: Which vitamin shortage is directly linked to poor blood clotting in long-term malabsorption?

options.A: Vitamin B1
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Vitamin A
options.D: Vitamin K

explanation: Vitamin K is a fat-soluble vitamin needed by the liver to make clotting factors. If fats aren't being absorbed, Vitamin K isn't either!

question: Why should you warn patients about mild side effects before they start a new drug?

options.A: To eliminate all possibility of severe allergic reactions developing later
options.B: To guarantee that the pharmacy receives full payment for the prescription
options.C: To prevent them from stopping the medication in panic when side effects occur
options.D: To ensure the patient stops taking the medication at the first sign of discomfort

explanation: A forewarned patient stays calm when mild side effects pop up and sticks to their treatment plan. Great patient education!

question: A nursing mother complains of extreme fatigue and a noticeable drop in milk supply after starting a very strict, low-calorie weight loss diet. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Inadequate daily caloric intake to support milk synthesis
options.B: A sudden hormonal imbalance unrelated to her food intake
options.C: Normal physiological changes that happen at three months postpartum
options.D: Drinking too much plain water instead of sugary beverages

explanation: Drastic calorie restriction robs the body of the energy required to make milk, leading to fatigue and reduced supply. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h2)

question: What is the primary job of ligaments in our joints?

options.A: To connect skeletal muscle directly to bone
options.B: To cushion the ends of bones from friction
options.C: To connect bone to bone and provide stability
options.D: To produce lubricating synovial fluid

explanation: Spot on! Ligaments are tough bands of tissue holding bones together so your joints stay stable when you move or carry weight.

question: How do corticosteroids stop swelling and inflammation in the body?

options.A: By blocking nerve impulses that transmit localized pain signals
options.B: By freezing cell membranes to prevent white blood cells from moving
options.C: By directly neutralizing circulating bacteria in the bloodstream
options.D: By altering DNA transcription to stop inflammatory chemical production

explanation: Steroids go right into cell nuclei to switch off the genes that create inflammatory chemicals. That's how they calm down swelling at the root!

question: Which secondary skin lesion looks like a narrow crack going down into the skin layer?

options.A: Fissure
options.B: Ulcer
options.C: Lichenification
options.D: Excoriation

explanation: Picture chapped lips or dry, cracked heels—that's a fissure. It's a sharp, linear crack in the skin.

question: Which tool involves community members drawing maps and calendars to show their own health and resource realities?

options.A: Private laboratory test reports
options.B: Standard hospital admission charts
options.C: Participatory Rural Appraisal (PRA)
options.D: National census questionnaires

explanation: PRA tools allow people to visually map their village resources and health risks themselves. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h6)

question: Who is considered the most central member of the home health care team?

options.A: The primary care physician
options.B: The patient and their family caregivers
options.C: The assigned physical therapist
options.D: The supervising registered nurse

explanation: Care happens in the home where the patient and family manage daily health needs, making them the core of the care team. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is the main goal of giving CPR to a patient?

options.A: To clear a blocked airway using forced abdominal thrusts
options.B: To cure the underlying cause of a sudden heart attack
options.C: To manually circulate oxygenated blood to vital organs
options.D: To restart a stopped heart using manual electric shocks

explanation: You're doing great! Remember that CPR doesn't usually restart the heart on its own. Instead, your hands act as a pump to keep oxygen flowing to the brain and heart until help arrives.

question: Why do nurses recommend using an ordinary cup instead of a feeding bottle for giving liquids to older infants?

options.A: Cups are much easier to clean and lower the risk of bacterial infections
options.B: Using bottles interferes with the natural development of the jawbone
options.C: Cups encourage the infant to drink larger volumes of liquid at one time
options.D: Infants cannot swallow liquids properly from a bottle after six months

explanation: Feeding bottles have tricky nooks and crannies that trap germs and are tough to sterilize. Cups are simple to wash and keep babies much safer from tummy bugs!

question: What is the main cause of Type 1 diabetes?

options.A: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells
options.B: Gradual resistance of body cells to normal insulin
options.C: Temporary hormone changes during pregnancy
options.D: Poor dietary intake of refined carbohydrates

explanation: In Type 1 diabetes, the body's immune system gets confused and mistakenly attacks the insulin-making beta cells in the pancreas. Brilliant to keep this distinction in mind!

question: How many loose or watery stools in a day is generally used to define diarrhoea?

options.A: Seven or more mucous stools per day
options.B: Five or more solid stools per day
options.C: Three or more loose stools per day
options.D: One or two hard stools per day

explanation: Passing three or more loose or watery bowel movements within 24 hours is the standard clinical sign that someone has diarrhoea. You've got this!

question: A patient asks how to lower their colon cancer risk through food. What is the best nursing advice?

options.A: Eliminate all forms of dietary fat from the daily menu
options.B: Eat more processed red meat and smoked foods daily
options.C: Increase intake of fresh vegetables and whole grains
options.D: Take high-dose iron supplements with every meal

explanation: Well done! Eating plenty of fiber-rich veggies and whole grains keeps the bowel healthy and protects against colon issues. Balance is key!

question: What is the main job of the intrinsic muscles found completely inside the tongue?

options.A: Supplying blood to the taste buds
options.B: Protruding the tongue out of the mouth
options.C: Changing the overall shape of the tongue
options.D: Anchoring the tongue to the mandible

explanation: Because intrinsic muscles live entirely inside the tongue, they work like a flexible cushion to change its shape when you talk or swallow.

question: Why should a nurse study local disease patterns before planning a health talk?

options.A: To fulfill a mandatory administrative file requirement for the federal ministry
options.B: To guarantee that every single household receives identical instructions
options.C: To ensure the teaching targets the actual health challenges facing that specific community
options.D: To prove that modern medicine is superior to traditional healing methods

explanation: Well done! Every community is unique. Knowing their specific challenges helps you focus on what actually matters to them.

question: Why is a slightly lower hemoglobin level accepted during the second trimester?

options.A: Maternal bone marrow becomes temporarily suppressed
options.B: Red blood cell production completely stops temporarily
options.C: Greater plasma volume expansion occurs during this period
options.D: Fetal iron demands are lowest at this stage of growth

explanation: Spot on! The body makes a lot more fluid (plasma) during the second trimester. This extra fluid dilutes the red blood cells, which naturally lowers the hemoglobin reading without meaning she's losing blood.

question: What does a drug overdose actually mean?

options.A: Taking two different drugs at the exact same time
options.B: Taking more than the recommended amount of a substance
options.C: Stopping a prescribed medication too suddenly
options.D: Experiencing a mild allergic reaction to a tablet

explanation: You've got this! An overdose simply happens when someone takes more of a drug than their body can safely handle and process at once.

question: A nurse wants to show the percentage breakdown of patient satisfaction ratings across four distinct wards. Which graph is most appropriate?

options.A: Pie chart
options.B: Scatter plot
options.C: Histogram
options.D: Line graph

explanation: Pie charts are ideal for displaying percentage shares of a whole, such as how different wards share out total satisfaction categories. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why can relying only on 'the way we've always done it' (clinical tradition) be tricky in healthcare?

options.A: It prevents nurses from communicating effectively with doctors
options.B: It causes immediate legal action against the hospital management
options.C: It automatically increases the cost of purchasing hospital equipment
options.D: It can keep outdated habits alive that no longer serve the patient well

explanation: Great job! Just because we've 'always done it that way' doesn't mean it's still the best way. Science and care methods keep improving for our patients' benefit.

question: What does the acronym VCT stand for in HIV nursing care?

options.A: Vaccination and Chemotherapy Therapy
options.B: Voluntary Counseling and Testing
options.C: Viral Care Treatment
options.D: Venereal Control Technique

explanation: VCT stands for Voluntary Counseling and Testing, a core strategy for encouraging people to know their HIV status confidentially. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T4#GNS214_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is a direct way to check the quality of youth-friendly services from the clients' own viewpoint?

options.A: Counting the number of chairs in the parking lot
options.B: Gathering feedback through exit interviews and suggestion boxes
options.C: Reading national textbooks on adult medicine
options.D: Checking the personal financial records of the nursing staff

explanation: Spot on! Asking the young clients directly via suggestion boxes or quick chats lets you know what's working and what needs fixing.

question: A patient with uncontrolled pain has a high heart rate and high blood pressure. Which system is causing this?

options.A: Peripheral nerve degeneration
options.B: Parasympathetic nervous system
options.C: Sympathetic nervous system
options.D: Thyroid hormone failure

explanation: Pain is stressful! It activates the sympathetic 'fight-or-flight' response, releasing hormones that speed up your heart and raise your blood pressure.

question: A patient with high blood pressure and high blood sugar is told to switch from white bread to whole grain bread. Why is this a great choice?

options.A: Refined white bread has no calories for the body to process
options.B: Whole grains retain fiber, which slows digestion and prevents sharp sugar spikes
options.C: Whole grains eliminate all fats from the patient's daily diet
options.D: Whole grains contain complete proteins that repair damaged blood vessels

explanation: You nailed it! The natural fiber in whole grains slows down how fast sugar enters the blood, keeping levels nice and steady.

question: How often should a nurse check a stable HIV patient's weight to catch any nutritional drops early?

options.A: At every clinic visit
options.B: Once every five years
options.C: Only after surgery
options.D: Only when they have a fever

explanation: You got it! Checking weight regularly helps you spot trouble before it turns into severe malnutrition or muscle wasting.

question: Why do myoblasts stop dividing before they fuse into myotubes?

options.A: To allow nerve endings to attach before the muscle membrane forms
options.B: Because the surrounding bone tissue physically blocks further cell division
options.C: To begin synthesizing contractile proteins and organizing into fibers
options.D: Because they run out of oxygen supply in the early embryo

explanation: Once they stop multiplying, the cells focus all their energy on building the proteins (like actin and myosin) needed for muscle contraction. Keep up the brilliant work!

question: A patient comes in complaining of light spotting between her periods and after sex. Which condition is most likely?

options.A: Uterine fibroid
options.B: Pelvic inflammatory disease
options.C: Ovarian cyst
options.D: Cervical polyp

explanation: Spotting between periods or right after intercourse is a classic giveaway for fragile cervical polyps!

question: Why is tele-nursing especially helpful for rural healthcare in Nigeria?

options.A: It lets nurses care for patients without forcing long, costly travel
options.B: It eliminates all expenses related to purchasing medical equipment
options.C: It guarantees uninterrupted electricity supply in remote villages
options.D: It completely replaces the need for physical hospitals everywhere

explanation: Spot on! Many patients in rural areas spend a lot of money and time just getting to a clinic. Tele-nursing brings basic nursing advice directly to them.

question: A patient loves the extra sympathy and gets excused from chores because of physical complaints that doctors can't find a medical cause for. What is this called?

options.A: Primary gain
options.B: Secondary gain
options.C: Cognitive dissonance
options.D: Neuroplasticity

explanation: Spot on! Secondary gain refers to the external perks—like extra care, sympathy, or getting out of house chores—that come along with playing the sick role.

question: Why can blood protein markers like albumin sometimes give misleading results during an infection?

options.A: Infection causes the liver to permanently stop producing all plasma proteins
options.B: Dehydration artificially raises albumin levels to mask underlying deficiencies
options.C: Inflammation lowers their levels independently of actual dietary protein intake
options.D: White blood cells consume circulating albumin for energy during fever

explanation: When the body is inflamed, it triggers an immune response that drops blood protein levels, even if the patient's diet is fine. Tricky, but good to know!

question: How would you best describe a 'nutrient'?

options.A: The total amount of food eaten in one day
options.B: A chemical compound in food needed for body function and repair
options.C: A manufactured vitamin pill taken during illness
options.D: Any liquid substance that quenches thirst

explanation: Nutrients are the tiny building blocks inside food that our bodies use to grow, repair tissues, and stay energized.

question: Why might a nursing student take a beta-blocker like propranolol before giving a major class presentation?

options.A: To increase their energy levels and stage presence
options.B: To cure their underlying social phobia permanently
options.C: To prevent them from falling asleep during the performance
options.D: To control physical symptoms like a racing heart and tremors

explanation: Beta-blockers block adrenaline, keeping your hands steady and heart calm without making your mind foggy. A real lifesaver for stage fright!

question: What is the main function of sticky chest electrodes in cardiac monitoring?

options.A: To warm up the chest skin for better blood circulation
options.B: To measure the exact temperature of the chest wall
options.C: To deliver mild electrical shocks to reset the rhythm
options.D: To pick up the electrical signals generated by the heart

explanation: Electrodes act as sensors that detect tiny electrical currents on the skin surface coming from the beating heart. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the main goal of giving Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) to someone with HIV?

options.A: To replace damaged CD4 cells with donor bone marrow
options.B: To suppress viral replication to undetectable levels
options.C: To cure opportunistic infections without antibiotics
options.D: To completely eradicate the virus from every body cell

explanation: ART stops the virus from multiplying, keeping viral counts super low and protecting the immune system.

question: A patient has a painful abscess right over the palm of their wrist, dangerously close to major nerves and blood vessels. What should you do first?

options.A: Apply hot compresses and send the patient home
options.B: Start high-dose oral antibiotics without any drainage
options.C: Immediately perform bedside incision and drainage
options.D: Refer the patient for specialized surgical evaluation

explanation: Hands and faces have delicate nerves and blood vessels. Abscesses in these tricky spots are best left to specialists to avoid accidental permanent injury.

question: Which common bacterial infection is famous for causing silent damage that can lead to infertility if ignored?

options.A: Candidiasis
options.B: Chlamydia
options.C: Pubic lice
options.D: Bacterial vaginosis

explanation: Chlamydia is often called a 'silent' infection because it sneaks in without symptoms while quietly harming the fallopian tubes.

question: How do nurses check for pain or nerve issues in a baby who cannot talk yet?

options.A: Measure their daily weight gain
options.B: Ask parents to translate facial expressions
options.C: Check muscle electricity with a monitor
options.D: Look for constant crying and restlessness

explanation: Babies can't tell us where it hurts, so we watch their mood! Inconsolable crying and fussiness are their way of saying something is wrong.

question: A rural community suffers from a high rate of waterborne diseases like cholera. Besides treating sick patients, which action represents true intersectoral collaboration?

options.A: Asking nurses to work overtime shifts in the treatment tent
options.B: Increasing the price of local river water to discourage drinking it
options.C: Ordering more intravenous fluids from the central medical store
options.D: Partnering with public works and local leaders to build safe boreholes

explanation: Working with public works engineers addresses the environmental source of the problem rather than just treating the resulting illness. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which harmful community myth do nurses need to actively correct during health talks?

options.A: That eating green vegetables can improve overall immune function
options.B: That breast cancer is caused by witchcraft or supernatural spells
options.C: That exercising regularly helps maintain a healthy body weight
options.D: That monthly self-examinations help women know their own bodies

explanation: Blaming curses or witchcraft is a dangerous myth that keeps people away from hospitals until it's too late. Education is our best weapon!

question: What is the main genetic material found inside the HIV virus?

options.A: Ribosomal RNA
options.B: Plasmid DNA
options.C: Single-stranded RNA
options.D: Double-stranded DNA

explanation: Think of HIV as an RNA virus! It carries two strands of single-stranded RNA, which it uses to make DNA once inside your body's cells. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U6_T2#GNS216_U6_T2_h1)

question: When is a public health nurse legally and ethically permitted to breach patient confidentiality?

options.A: When the local newspaper offers financial payment for health records
options.B: When the patient's condition poses an immediate and severe threat to public safety
options.C: Whenever a curious neighbor asks about someone's medical diagnosis
options.D: Whenever the nurse feels like gossiping during lunch break

explanation: Confidentiality is a sacred duty, but protecting the public from severe, imminent harm overrides individual privacy rights under specific legal guidelines. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h8)

question: Why should a home health nurse document environmental hazards like poor lighting or uneven floors?

options.A: These factors directly influence client safety and risk of injury
options.B: Insurance companies use this data to calculate property taxes
options.C: Building inspectors require nurses to enforce local housing laws
options.D: It proves the nurse inspected the neighborhood security system

explanation: Environmental conditions in a home directly impact clinical outcomes, such as increasing the risk of falls for an elderly client. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is the usual maximum safe volume of fluid for one subcutaneous injection in an adult?

options.A: Any volume ordered by the doctor
options.B: Up to 0.5 mL to 1.5 mL
options.C: Between 5 mL and 10 mL
options.D: Exactly 3.0 mL to 5.0 mL

explanation: Keeping subcutaneous volumes small (under 1.5 mL) keeps the patient comfortable and prevents painful swelling in that little pocket of fat.

question: Which sign should you teach a mother to report immediately after taking her baby home from a circumcision?

options.A: The baby is unable to pass urine for many hours after the procedure
options.B: The baby cries briefly when the diaper is changed
options.C: A thin yellowish film is visible on the surface of the glans penis
options.D: The Plastibell ring is still attached on the third day at home

explanation: If a baby can't pee, it could mean swelling is blocking the urethra. That's an urgent sign that needs immediate medical review!

question: Why must a nurse shake a suspension oral medication before pouring a dose?

options.A: To create bubbles that improve the taste
options.B: To warm the liquid up to body temperature
options.C: To evenly redistribute the settled drug particles
options.D: To activate the chemical preservatives inside

explanation: Suspensions contain solid particles that naturally settle at the bottom of the container, so shaking ensures the patient gets the correct dose strength. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h3)

question: How would you describe an 'asymptomatic carrier' to a fellow nursing student?

options.A: An individual who is currently experiencing severe symptoms of disease
options.B: A person who carries a pathogen without showing any signs of illness
options.C: A patient who has fully recovered and no longer sheds any germs
options.D: A healthcare worker who always wears proper personal protective equipment

explanation: Asymptomatic means no symptoms! They carry the germ around and feel totally fine, which is why infection control can be tricky.

question: Why are mass measles vaccinations carried out right away when a new IDP camp opens?

options.A: Measles vaccine protects adults from chronic joint pain
options.B: Crowded camp conditions make measles outbreaks highly likely and deadly
options.C: Measles is transmitted exclusively through contaminated river water
options.D: Local health authorities require it to issue food rations

explanation: Measles spreads like wildfire in crowded places and can be fatal for undernourished children, so early vaccination saves lives.

question: Which chart is best for tracking clinical data points over time?

options.A: Anatomical diagram
options.B: Organizational chart
options.C: Run chart
options.D: Pie chart

explanation: Think of a run chart as a story running across time. It helps us easily spot if things are going up, down, or staying steady week by week.

question: Which sterilization method is best suited for sharp surgical blades because it prevents them from dulling?

options.A: Boiling water for twenty minutes
options.B: Dry heat in a hot air oven
options.C: High-pressure steam autoclave
options.D: Cold soaking in mild soap water

explanation: Dry heat does not cause rust or water-related dulling, making it ideal for maintaining the sharp edges of surgical blades. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of a nasogastric tube?

options.A: To provide continuous oxygen to the lungs
options.B: To deliver liquid nutrients directly into the stomach
options.C: To drain excess urine from the bladder
options.D: To remove harmful toxins from the bloodstream

explanation: A nasogastric tube is passed through the nose into the stomach to supply food and medications when a patient cannot swallow safely. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of surgical asepsis compared to medical asepsis?

options.A: To replace the need for routine hand washing
options.B: To keep hospital room surfaces smelling fresh
options.C: To eliminate all microorganisms and spores completely
options.D: To reduce the number of visible dirt particles on skin

explanation: Surgical asepsis creates a sterile environment free of all life forms, including resistant bacterial spores, unlike medical asepsis which only reduces pathogen counts. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of writing an incident report when a medical error or near-miss happens?

options.A: To find someone to blame and punish immediately
options.B: To increase paperwork for the nursing administration
options.C: To hide the mistake from the hospital management
options.D: To find root causes and prevent future occurrences

explanation: Spot on! Incident reports are learning tools to improve system safety, not weapons to punish individual nurses.

question: Which cells in the male testes are stimulated by LH to produce testosterone?

options.A: Stem cells
options.B: Sertoli cells
options.C: Leydig cells
options.D: Thyroid cells

explanation: Great job! Luteinizing hormone (LH) targets the Leydig cells in the testes to tell them to make testosterone.

question: Out of the common types of vaginitis, which one is officially classified as a sexually transmitted infection (STI)?

options.A: Atrophic vaginitis
options.B: Trichomoniasis
options.C: Vulvovaginal candidiasis
options.D: Bacterial vaginosis

explanation: Trichomoniasis is caused by a tiny parasite and is primarily passed along through sexual contact. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h2)

question: Long ago, during the demonological era, what did people generally believe caused mental illness?

options.A: Demonic possession and evil spirits
options.B: Severe vitamin deficiencies
options.C: Chemical imbalances in the brain
options.D: Hereditary genetic mutations

explanation: Before medical science grew, people didn't understand mental health issues yet, so they blamed unusual behaviors on spirits or supernatural forces. You've got this!

question: Why do different health workers come together as a team in community health?

options.A: To address complex health and social needs
options.B: To place full control of care on physicians
options.C: To reduce the number of working nurses
options.D: To lower the cost of running hospital wards

explanation: You've got this! Community health involves many overlapping social and physical issues, so different experts team up to tackle them all together.

question: A rural health clinic in Nigeria runs out of basic antibiotics due to weak local distribution. Which national strategy is failing in this specific instance?

options.A: The regulation of surgical equipment manufacturing standards
options.B: The curriculum used to train primary school teachers
options.C: The Essential Drug Policy supply chain and distribution network
options.D: The enforcement of international luxury hotel taxation

explanation: Stockouts at rural clinics highlight flaws in the procurement and distribution mechanisms outlined by the national drug policy. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h6)

question: Where and when was the global declaration reaffirming primary health care signed to mark the 40th anniversary of Alma-Ata?

options.A: Lagos, 1987
options.B: New York, 2015
options.C: Astana, 2018
options.D: Geneva, 2000

explanation: The Astana Declaration was adopted in Kazakhstan in 2018 to revitalize global commitment to primary health care. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is writing clear, real-time notes so important in emergency nursing?

options.A: It provides a clear legal record of all care provided
options.B: Doctors use the nurse's notes to diagnose diseases
options.C: It replaces the need for verbal shift handovers
options.D: It guarantees that the hospital insurance claim gets paid

explanation: Good documentation protects your patient's ongoing care and acts as legal proof in court of the great nursing care you delivered.

question: Besides published research, what else does evidence-based nursing practice bring together?

options.A: Superstition and historical habits
options.B: Personal intuition and strict tradition
options.C: Clinical expertise and patient preferences
options.D: Hospital budgets and physician seniority

explanation: Good evidence-based practice blends the best research with your own clinical judgment and what matters most to the patient.

question: Why do teenagers often take sudden risks without fully thinking things through?

options.A: They lack basic formal education regarding physical danger
options.B: The brain area for impulse control matures slower than the reward center
options.C: They have lower overall physical strength and poor balance
options.D: The visual cortex fails to judge speed and distance properly

explanation: Spot on! There is a developmental gap: the emotional reward center grows faster than the prefrontal cortex, which handles impulse control and long-term thinking.

question: What is cor pulmonale?

options.A: Infection of the heart valves resulting from severe pneumonia
options.B: Narrowing of the coronary arteries due to chronic low blood oxygen
options.C: Weakening of the left ventricle caused by systemic high blood pressure
options.D: Right heart failure caused by primary lung or pulmonary vascular disease

explanation: Spot on! Cor pulmonale happens when lung problems create high pressure in the pulmonary vessels, forcing the right side of the heart to struggle and eventually fail. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h6)

question: A patient asks why their shoulder can move in circles while their elbow can only bend and straighten. What is the best way to explain this?

options.A: The elbow contains more synovial fluid
options.B: The shoulder has much stronger muscles
options.C: The different shapes of the joint structures control the movement
options.D: The shoulder has softer bones than the elbow

explanation: You got it! Structure dictates function. A ball-and-socket shape lets the shoulder rotate, while a hinge shape restricts the elbow to one plane.

question: What is a major focus of care right after a child's heartbeat and breathing return (after ROSC)?

options.A: Discontinuing all cardiac and respiratory monitoring
options.B: Minimizing secondary brain injury and multi-organ damage
options.C: Withholding all fluids to prevent fluid overload
options.D: Allowing the child's body temperature to rise unchecked

explanation: Getting their pulse back is a huge win, but the job isn't done! Now we have to protect their organs—especially the brain—from further stress and damage.

question: Which drug tragedy in the 1950s and 1960s caused severe birth defects and completely changed global drug safety rules?

options.A: Sulfanilamide
options.B: Thalidomide
options.C: Penicillin
options.D: Paracetamol

explanation: Spot on! Thalidomide was prescribed for morning sickness back then, but it sadly caused severe limb defects in babies, forcing the world to tighten up drug safety laws.

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with a minor skin rash and no other symptoms. What triage category do they most likely belong to?

options.A: Resuscitation
options.B: Non-urgent
options.C: Emergent
options.D: Immediate

explanation: A simple rash without other symptoms does not threaten life or limb, placing it safely in the non-urgent category. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T1#GNS315_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is a major challenge when a hospital uses a cloud-based EHR system?

options.A: Nurses are completely barred from updating vital signs during the night shift
options.B: Hospital IT staff must manually replace internal hard drives every week
options.C: Patient records cannot be viewed outside the main hospital pharmacy
options.D: The system requires a stable, continuous internet connection to access patient files

explanation: Spot on! Cloud software lives online, so if the internet goes down, checking patient files can become a headache.

question: Which of these is a major barrier to nursing research in busy hospitals?

options.A: Excessive amounts of free time during shifts
options.B: Too many available financial grants and computers
options.C: Heavy clinical workloads and staffing shortages
options.D: Strict bans on publishing local healthcare data

explanation: Spot on! When nurse-to-patient ratios are high and everyone is exhausted, it's really tough to find the energy or time for research. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why does the baby have to make 'cardinal movements' while coming down the birth canal?

options.A: To stimulate the release of oxytocin from the maternal pituitary gland
options.B: To speed up the latent phase of the first stage of labour
options.C: To prevent the umbilical cord from wrapping around the baby's neck
options.D: To help the fetal head fit through the changing shapes of the maternal pelvis

explanation: The pelvis isn't a straight pipe! The baby has to twist and turn to navigate the different curves safely.

question: What do we call a sudden spike in disease cases that goes way above the normal baseline in a region?

options.A: Pandemic
options.B: Epidemic
options.C: Sporadic
options.D: Endemic

explanation: When an illness suddenly surges and hits way more people than usual in an area, that's an epidemic. Great job keeping these terms straight!

question: How does untreated cervicitis affect a patient's risk of contracting HIV?

options.A: It grants temporary immunity against sexually transmitted viruses.
options.B: It decreases the risk because white blood cells destroy the virus.
options.C: It increases the risk because the mucosal tissue is broken and immune cells are rushed to the area.
options.D: It has no measurable impact on viral transmission rates.

explanation: Inflamed, fragile tissue plus a gathering of immune cells gives viruses like HIV an easier pathway into the body.

question: What defines a mass casualty incident (MCI)?

options.A: An emergency that only happens inside a surgical theatre
options.B: A routine medical ward shift with high patient turnover
options.C: Any situation where a single patient arrives in an ambulance
options.D: Patient numbers and injuries overwhelm available local resources

explanation: An MCI happens when the scale of the emergency outstrips the normal staff, space, and supplies of the hospital or clinic. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T1#GNS315_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why should a patient hold their breath for a few seconds after puffing their inhaler medication?

options.A: To allow the drug particles time to settle deep into the small airways
options.B: To prevent the medication from reaching the stomach and causing ulcers
options.C: To ensure that all excess carbon dioxide is pushed out of the blood
options.D: To force the heart rate to slow down after deep inspiration

explanation: Holding the breath gives gravity and time for those tiny medicine particles to land right where they are needed in the lungs, instead of just being breathed right back out!

question: In developing areas, which social issue is most tied to high rates of teenage pregnancy?

options.A: Excessive participation in competitive sports
options.B: Poverty and lack of access to education
options.C: High rates of urban migration
options.D: Universal access to family planning clinics

explanation: Correct! Poverty and limited schooling often strip young girls of choices and keep them from knowing about or getting preventive reproductive care.

question: What should the treatment team do if a patient experiences behavioral instability during trial leave?

options.A: Ban the family from ever visiting again
options.B: Immediately discharge the patient permanently as a penalty
options.C: Ignore the incident and pretend the leave went smoothly
options.D: Analyze the triggers, adjust the care plan, and postpone further leave until stable

explanation: A rough patch isn't a failure—it's valuable feedback! It helps the team adjust the care plan before trying community living again.

question: What does the abbreviation WASH stand for in public health programs?

options.A: Widespread Access to Safety Hormones
options.B: Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene
options.C: Weekly Anti-mosquito Spraying Hazard
options.D: Wound Assessment and Surgical Health

explanation: WASH programs focus on clean drinking water, proper sanitation facilities, and personal hygiene education to prevent infectious diseases. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of nursing research informatics?

options.A: Managing daily staff shift rosters and nurse-to-patient ratios
options.B: Supporting data collection and analysis to discover new nursing knowledge
options.C: Ordering routine hospital supplies and medical equipment inventory
options.D: Providing health tips and reminders to patients via mobile phones

explanation: Research informatics uses technology to manage studies, analyze data, and build the evidence base for nursing practice. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T2#GNS113_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which skin change is a classic sign of long-term chronic venous insufficiency?

options.A: Shiny, hairless skin with thick toenails on the toes
options.B: Painful black sores right on the tips of the heels
options.C: Pale, cool skin that turns white instantly when lifted
options.D: Brownish skin discoloration and irritation around the ankles

explanation: High pressure in the lower leg veins forces tiny red blood cells to leak out into the skin. When they break down, they leave behind a rusty brown stain called hemosiderin.

question: Why do you need to work with an occupational therapist before a patient gets an automated wheelchair?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial cost for hospital billing
options.B: To ensure the wheelchair matches the room color scheme
options.C: To train the nursing staff on physical lifting techniques
options.D: To evaluate if the patient has the cognitive and motor skills to steer safely

explanation: Exactly right! We need to make sure the patient can safely control the powered chair so they don't accidentally run into walls or hurt anyone.

question: Nursing informatics is a blend of three major fields. Which ones are they?

options.A: Biology, chemistry, and clinical medicine
options.B: Pharmacology, anatomy, and health administration
options.C: Nursing science, computer science, and information science
options.D: Psychology, sociology, and data technology

explanation: Spot on! Nursing informatics brings together patient care, computers, and data management to make healthcare smoother and safer for everyone.

question: Why would a nurse researcher go for a correlational design?

options.A: To randomly assign patients to different hospital diets
options.B: To prove that variable A causes variable B to change
options.C: To test the effectiveness of a brand-new surgical tool
options.D: To explore the relationship between two existing variables

explanation: You got it! Correlation checks how two things relate to each other (like stress and lack of sleep), without claiming one directly causes the other.

question: As a nurse, what is the main goal of gender-transformative healthcare?

options.A: To prevent teenagers from ever talking about relationships
options.B: To focus exclusively on male patients during clinic hours
options.C: To actively challenge harmful norms while improving health access
options.D: To enforce traditional cultural rules inside hospital wards

explanation: Brilliant! This approach doesn't just treat the medical issue; it tackles the underlying social unfairness causing the health problem in the first place.

question: What is the absolute first thing a nurse checks during an initial trauma assessment?

options.A: Pain assessment
options.B: Airway management
options.C: Wound dressing
options.D: Checking blood pressure

explanation: Think ABCs! Keeping the airway open is always step one because a blocked airway causes a patient to deteriorate the fastest.

question: Why is keeping a close eye on vital signs so crucial when a patient is going through alcohol or sedative withdrawal?

options.A: It helps prove to the patient that they have an active drug problem
options.B: It replaces the need to take blood samples for kidney function tests
options.C: Withdrawal from these substances can cause dangerous and life-threatening physical instability
options.D: Vital signs remain completely normal throughout the entire detox process

explanation: Spot on! Unlike some other substances, alcohol and sedative withdrawal can trigger severe seizures and drastic blood pressure changes. Close monitoring keeps the patient safe.

question: In some traditional Nigerian settings, how might hiring a paid home care nurse be viewed by the community?

options.A: As the cheapest way to manage chronic illness
options.B: As a mandatory legal requirement for all households
options.C: As a government-sponsored welfare program
options.D: As a sign of abandoning family care duties

explanation: You got it! Culturally, people sometimes wrongly assume hiring a nurse means you are neglecting your sick family member.

question: Why do nurses need to keep cultural and religious beliefs in mind when giving diet advice?

options.A: Because cultural beliefs completely override all biological needs for protein
options.B: Because hospital regulations require patients to follow traditional holiday menus
options.C: Because religious leaders must personally approve every prescribed hospital meal
options.D: Because food consumption habits are deeply tied to tradition, identity, and social norms

explanation: Food is tied to who we are. If you ignore cultural traditions, patients simply won't follow your nutrition advice.

question: What is the main job of agar in microbiology culture media?

options.A: To solidify liquid broth into a solid growth surface
options.B: To lower the temperature inside laboratory incubators
options.C: To provide extra oxygen for anaerobic bacteria
options.D: To stain bacterial cells under a light microscope

explanation: You nailed it! Agar comes from seaweed and acts like gelatin, turning liquid broth into a firm plate where colonies can grow nicely.

question: How would you score a patient who speaks in full sentences, but insists they are in a different city and year?

options.A: Incomprehensible sounds
options.B: Confused conversation
options.C: Inappropriate words
options.D: Oriented and alert

explanation: Even though they are talking in sentences, getting the place and time wrong means they are confused. They get a verbal score of 4 for confused conversation.

question: What happens to a mother's body stores if her diet lacks certain essential nutrients while she is breastfeeding?

options.A: The chemical composition of her milk changes to match her poor diet
options.B: Her baby stops growing immediately due to a sudden lack of calories
options.C: Her body draws from its own tissue stores to keep the milk nutritious
options.D: Milk production stops completely until her diet improves

explanation: Maternal physiology prioritizes infant nutrition, often depleting maternal reserves like bone calcium if dietary intake is insufficient. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h1)

question: A client returns complaining of annoying, continuous spotting two months after her implant insertion. What is your best first nursing action?

options.A: Insist that she has an undiagnosed infection and prescribe strong broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Validate her experience, explain that irregular bleeding is a known side effect, and offer treatment options
options.C: Tell her the implant is defective and demand that she undergo immediate emergency surgery
options.D: Advise her to stop drinking water for three days to dry up her internal hormonal secretions

explanation: Always listen with empathy! Reassuring her that spotting is normal and offering management options helps her feel supported and confident.

question: What is the main difference between a theoretical and a conceptual framework?

options.A: A theoretical framework is based on an established grand theory
options.B: A conceptual framework is never used in nursing research
options.C: A conceptual framework has no variables attached to it
options.D: A theoretical framework is created only by students

explanation: Theoretical frameworks lean on big, already-tested theories (like Nightingale's theory), while conceptual frameworks are often built from scratch for your specific study.

question: Why are transcutaneous (skin) bilirubin readings often followed up with a blood test when numbers are high?

options.A: Skin devices can be influenced by skin tone and are only meant for screening
options.B: Transcutaneous meters measure direct bilirubin instead of total bilirubin
options.C: Skin readings only work accurately after the baby is two weeks old
options.D: Blood tests are required by law before a baby can start breastfeeding

explanation: Handheld skin scanners are wonderful for quick checks, but a blood test gives us the exact numbers needed for treatment decisions.

question: Why is it smart for a nurse manager to catch early warning signs instead of waiting for a big formal complaint?

options.A: It proves to the hospital director that the shift is running perfectly
options.B: It allows the manager to punish the guilty nurses immediately
options.C: It ensures that hospital management never has to spend money on training
options.D: It gives the manager a chance to step in before the atmosphere turns toxic

explanation: Catching small tensions early lets you talk it out before it explodes into a major drama that disrupts patient care.

question: A patient asks why they need to stay lying down for 15 minutes after getting a suppository. What is your best response?

options.A: To help the digestive system push the drug up into the stomach
options.B: To allow the blood pressure to drop safely back to normal levels
options.C: To ensure the patient falls asleep quickly and rests comfortably
options.D: To prevent the medication from being pushed out before it dissolves

explanation: Staying flat gives the medicine time to melt and absorb into the lining instead of sliding right back out.

question: Nigerian staple foods like yam and cassava are famous for giving us a massive supply of which macronutrient?

options.A: Complete proteins
options.B: Fat-soluble vitamins
options.C: Carbohydrates
options.D: Essential fatty acids

explanation: Exactly! Root crops and cereals like yam and cassava are our powerhouse sources of carbohydrates, giving our bodies the energy we need every day.

question: Why do hospitals still rely on high-temperature incineration for certain waste, despite environmental concerns?

options.A: It is the only method permitted for ordinary kitchen food leftovers
options.B: It transforms dangerous clinical trash into reusable office furniture
options.C: It requires zero financial investment to build and maintain
options.D: It completely destroys difficult pathological waste and reduces overall volume

explanation: Some body tissues and heavy clinical waste need intense heat to completely and permanently wipe out disease risks.

question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a secondary (acquired) immunodeficiency?

options.A: Suppression caused by chemotherapy drugs
options.B: A genetic enzyme defect present since birth
options.C: Immune damage resulting from an HIV infection
options.D: Malnutrition leading to weakened white blood cell function

explanation: A condition present right from birth is a primary (congenital) issue. Conditions like HIV, malnutrition, and chemo damage a previously healthy immune system later in life, making them acquired.

question: Which statistical test is frequently used for categorical data in cross-sectional studies?

options.A: Chi-square test
options.B: Longitudinal growth curve
options.C: Surgical survival analysis
options.D: Cellular mitosis assay

explanation: When working with categories (like gender or disease status), the chi-square test is the classic statistical tool to check for links.

question: Where is the best place to put visual reminders for a new clinical practice?

options.A: Inside the locked office of the hospital director
options.B: On the bulletin board outside the hospital gates
options.C: Right where the clinical action actually happens
options.D: Inside the main staff cafeteria next to the coffee machine

explanation: Putting prompts directly at the point of care, like on medication trolleys, ensures staff see them when they need them most. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary focus of dietary counselling?

options.A: Handing out strict meal plans that patients must memorize
options.B: Guiding food choices to promote health and manage illness
options.C: Prescribing high-dose vitamin supplements for fatigue
options.D: Diagnosing rare metabolic disorders using blood tests
